Sound is measured by its frequency, in units called Hertz (Hz). The higher the frequency, the sharper or more high-pitched the sound appears.

A Tone block can play the same sound as a Note block by using the right sound frequency. 


Using the Tone block, play a C4 note for 2 seconds.
The Tone frequency of a C4 note is 262Hz.

Sound is measured by its frequency, in units called Hertz (Hz). The higher the frequency, the sharper or more high-pitched the sound appears.

The Tone block allows you to play a wider range of sounds (up to 8000Hz with the block).

We can make interesting sound effects using a quick sequence of tones. The quality of the speaker makes a difference to the sound effect. The physical robot has a weaker speaker and thus it does not sound as clear as that of the virtual robot, which uses the computer speaker.  



Try out this sound effect:
  1. Play a sequence of 5 sounds using Tone blocks.
  2. Set the duration of all the blocks to 0.1 second.
  3. Use the frequencies in order: 500Hz, 8000Hz, 600Hz, 1000Hz, 2000Hz.
  4. Test on both physical robot and virtual robot to hear the difference.

Below is a part of the music score for Twinkle Twinkle Little Star.



Use your robot to play the tune using Tone blocks. Note that it sounds better with the virtual robot.

Set the duration of each note to 1 second and use a wait interval of 0.1 second between the notes. 

The frequencies for the musical notes are as follows:
